newsitem.title: USA: Califoria man escapes prison to kill spouse.
newsitem.headline: Califoria man escapes prison to kill spouse.

text.p: A California man in prison for spousal abuse escaped Tuesday, returning home to kill the woman he lived with, authorities said.
He then kidnapped his 6-year-old daughter and fled before he was killed by police later that day.
Michael Stalworth, 27, escaped from the low-security Elk Grove jail near Sacramento early Tuesday morning, John McGinness of the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office said.
Stalworth then went to a house in a Sacramento suburb where he had lived with a 27-year-old woman, whose name was not released. McGinness said he was not certain if the couple was married.
Stalworth had been in jail since March 21 after being convicted of abusing the woman, McGinness said. He was due for release in November.

The woman was out when Stalworth returned, but he was waiting when she drove up the street, McGinness said. The woman apparently tried to escape, crashing into a fence. Stalworth allegedly fired several shots, killing her, McGinness said.
Stalworth then took the couple's daughter from the passenger seat of the car, commandeered a vehicle and later switched to another car, McGinness said.
Authorities issued an all-points bulletin for Stalworth, who was later spotted in the car in Stockton, 50 miles south of Sacramento, officials said.

San Joaquin County sheriff's deputies followed the vehicle for a short distance before Stalworth stopped at the home of a relative in Stockton, Stockton police spokesman Ken Praegitzer said. Stalworth got out of the car armed with a pistol and walked toward the front door of the house, Praegitzer said.

"The deputies ordered him to stop and drop the weapon. At the front door there was a confrontation between the deputies and the suspect ... Several shots were fired. The suspect was hit and died at the scene," Praegitzer said.
No sheriff's deputies were injured, he said.
Before the shooting, Stalworth dropped off his daughter in Stockton and she was unharmed, Praegitzer said.
